title: Fault robustness: nominal vs fault-aware supervision under identical injected failures
research_question: Under identical injected sensor, actuation, communication, software and physical faults, does a fault-aware supervisor (validation, residual CUSUM, degradation estimate, recovery modes, independent safety filter) reduce temperature violations relative to a nominal supervisor, how fast does it detect and recover, and what does the caution cost?
hypothesis: S6 scenario at 38 C ambient, load 0.6, 2 h, dynamic loop (40 kg, 1 K/min), RTX-world parameters (as E015). Controllers joint_meas and mpc, each under a nominal supervisor (catches exceptions, holds the last action) and a fault-aware supervisor. Window faults from 2400 to 4200 s: sensor dropout (junction and supply NaN), junction bias -10 K, stuck sensors, clock commands not applied, communication failure (telemetry frozen, commands lost), controller crash, solver infeasibility, supply-sensor bias -8 K. Physical faults unknown to the controller: 600 s setpoint delay, +0.02 K/W fouling step at 2400 s, degraded pump (flow capped at 0.6, efficiency 0.35), wrong model (controller's r_cond 0.024 vs true 0.04). H1: with no fault, the fault-aware supervisor raises no alarm in any run and its energy per success is within 0.5% of the nominal stack's for both controllers (seed means). H2: for the 8 window faults, the first alarm comes at or after onset and within 180 s (3 control intervals) in at least 80% of fault-aware runs (both controllers pooled). H3: for every fault and both controllers, fault-aware chip-seconds above t_target are at most the nominal stack's plus 1 chip-second (seed means). H4: for clock_stuck, fault-aware reduces chip-seconds above t_target by at least 50% relative to nominal for each controller where nominal's mean is above 0. H5: after window faults, the fault-aware supervisor is back in NORMAL mode within 300 s of the fault ending in at least 80% of the runs in which it left NORMAL. H6: for fouling, degraded pump and wrong model, the degradation detector alarms (at or after onset) in at least 80% of fault-aware runs. Descriptive: energy cost of fault-awareness per fault, late tasks, throttled chip-seconds, false alarms before onset.
null_hypothesis: Fault-aware supervision does not reduce temperature violations and detects faults no faster than chance.
baseline: nominal supervisor with the same controller
evaluation_criteria: Seed means for violations and fractions; detection delay = first alarm - onset; paired relative differences with 95% t-CI for energy.
sample_size: 5 seeds x 13 faults x 4 policy stacks = 260 runs.
randomization: Workloads drawn per seed, shared across faults and stacks.
measurement_boundary: Simulated single-node facility (as E015); faults are injected in simulation only.
known_limitations: Fault set and magnitudes chosen by hand; CUSUM learning window assumed fault-free (physical faults present from t = 0 are learned as baseline and only the resistance estimator can see them); one scenario; joint_meas does not use junction readings, so junction-sensor faults cannot hurt it (a property, not an artefact). Crash and infeasibility are both injected as exceptions for joint_meas.
known_confounders: fault-aware SAFE mode raises cooling energy; energy differences mix caution with fault effects
disclosure: Before registration, smoke runs (seed 0, 2 h, both controllers) of faults none, dropout, supply bias, stale, clock_stuck and crash: no false alarm without a fault after a start-up fix; clock_stuck gave 515 (joint_meas) and 1224 (mpc) chip-seconds above target nominal vs 73 and 135 fault-aware; dropout cost the fault-aware joint_meas stack ~23% energy per success; a supply bias of -8 K gave mpc 18 chip-seconds above target nominal vs 0 fault-aware. Detector thresholds were fixed before E019 and not tuned on these runs (the CUSUM was made more conservative after a unit test on synthetic Gaussian residuals showed false alarms). No E019 cell was run before registration.
data_collection: Append-only store; supervisor diagnostics stored as diag_* metrics.
statistics: Seed means; detection and recovery as run fractions; paired t-CI for energy.
